result:
**Round 312 verdict: FAIL**, but the cause is one Medium problem in the perf test harness, not in A's app code. Every app-code check passed, so B should not send the app work back to A.

**What passed in real Chromium**, compared against a HEAD copy of `store/` running on port 5174:
- **Main thread (3 loads):** no peaks computation on the main thread on any load, and `peaks.worker.ts` is created once per load. HEAD spends 39–56 ms in `computePeaks`.
- **Waveforms:** the 9 library previews are byte-identical to HEAD. So are all 9 clip waveforms and the detail waveforms after adding every sound with Enter, at 1440×900 and 1280×720, before and after zooming in twice.
- **Ready order:** the first frame that says "Demo collection ready" already has its preview drawn. No library sound became addable before its peaks arrived from the worker.
- **Video import (`1.mp4`):** the audio waveform and the status lines match HEAD.
- **Copy size:** every copy into the worker is at most 2 seconds of audio (96,000 samples at 48 kHz). The copies take 12.4 ms per load in total.
- **Leaving mid-load:** navigating away while the worker was busy shut the worker down. Coming back loaded all 9 waves unchanged, with no page errors.
- **Premium auth is not bypassed (both viewports):** `/studio-lab` opens the demo with no user signed in. `/studio/middle-east` asks for sign-in and loads no audio. `/api/studio-token` returns 401 without a sign-in header and no token in any response.
- **Offline checks:** the file changes match the task exactly (only the 2 allowed files modified, 5 new files), the claims script output matches, the 119 covering unit tests pass, and the implementation doc meets its spec.
- **Mutation tests:** all 17 of A's mutants failed the tests again on my own scratch copy, as they should. Two of my own also failed. Of the four that survived, two make no behavioural difference. The other two confirm a known A review finding (A-R312-REVIEW-L4): nothing tests the video call site's guard, and nothing catches a stall timer that is armed only at the start of a job.

**C-R312-01 (Medium): the perf harness spec now fails.**
- **What happens:** `perf/studio-lab.perf.spec.ts`, run alone, failed on A's tree in both runs with "no long-animation-frame entry carried script timings". The same spec passed on the HEAD copy.
- **Why:** moving the peaks off the main thread removed the last long frame from the normal-speed page load. The harness treats "no long frames at all" as broken instrumentation, so `load.script-max` now reads 0 and proves nothing.
- **Who fixes it:** A was not allowed to edit `perf/**`, and B's pre-check never ran this spec on the sketch. B needs to rule on the harness check and allow edits to `perf/lib/report.ts`.
- **Why it matters:** the root gate doesn't run this spec, so the problem would otherwise go unnoticed and block the measurement tool for every later performance round.

**Also for B:**
- Doc 228 line 4 says "C round 312 PASS", as the task required. That line is wrong while this round is FAIL, so the fix-up should correct it.
- The first auth-check run timed out because the server was cold. I kept it as an invalid environment attempt and the rerun after a warm-up passed.

`browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true, because all 8 required browser checks ran. Full vitest, build, Biome, `npm run verify` and the e2e smoke test are left to the root gate. I changed no app source; the only side effects are the git-ignored `store/build` and `store/test-results` from the perf runs.

Everything is in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- c-round-312.md
- c-round-312.json
- c-round-312/ (logs, JSON results, mutants and screenshots; `c-browse.json` is in this folder)
